item.title: LAMal awards in Valais: bands and reductions 2026
item.description: Guide to compulsory sick pay premiums in the canton of Valais: deductibles available, insurance models, premium reduction and procedure for obtaining cantonal subsidies.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - LAMal is mandatory in Valais with premiums varying by age and insurance model - Available deductibles: from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 for adults - Premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy for low- to middle-income families - Deadline for changing health insurance: December 31 of the previous year
## Key facts - **What**: Mandatory health insurance (LAMal) with per capita premiums and variable deductibles - Where: Canton of Valais; mandatory for residents domiciled in the canton - Who: All residents; mandatory within 3 months of arrival - When: Annual premiums; change of insurance company by December 31 for effect from January 1 - Models: Basic insurance, HMO, network, models with high deductible - Deductibles: CHF 300, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500 for adults - Subsidies: Premium reduction managed by the canton of Valais for income and asset brackets
In the canton of Valais, as in the rest of Switzerland, the mandatory health insurance (LAMal) covers residents and foreigners domiciled in any canton. Premiums are managed at the cantonal-regional level and vary based on age brackets, chosen insurance models, and deductibles. Valais, like every canton, has a premium reduction system (cantonal subsidy) aimed at families that do not reach certain income levels.
The system's structure is private: health insurance companies operate with per capita premiums (i.e., calculated for each individual), NOT as a salary contribution or tax. This means that each family member pays their own premium, regardless of age or economic condition — except for cantonal subsidies for low incomes.
### Premium brackets and deductibles in Valais
In the canton of Valais, several health insurance companies operate. Premiums are communicated annually by individual insurers and registered at the cantonal level. For adults, the available deductibles are six: CHF 300, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, and 2,500. A higher deductible (e.g., 2,500) results in a lower monthly premium, as the insured accepts to cover a larger share of healthcare costs before the insurance kicks in.
Children benefit from separate deductibles, generally more favorable than those for adults. Mandatory LAMal includes basic coverage (essential services: hospital, outpatient medicine, drugs, maternity, accidents for those without separate accident insurance). On this basis, additional optional coverages (dentist, physiotherapy, alternative medicines) can be added — optional and NOT regulated by LAMal.
Keyword: the premium is PER CAPITA. If a family of four resides in Valais, they will pay four separate premiums (one for each member), even if they choose the same deductible and the same health insurance company.
[Compare health insurance companies and LAMal premiums for your profile](nav:health) The reduction of premiums (cantonal subsidy) is a crucial tool for families and self-employed workers with limited income. In the canton of Valais, as in almost all cantons, the responsible cantonal authority evaluates the total income of the household (cantonal taxable income, possibly adjusted) and the assets, and grants a monthly contribution that directly reduces the LAMal premium due.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Procedure to obtain the premium reduction
Those living in the canton of Valais and with a low to medium income should consult the cantonal office responsible for social services or health. In Valais, the competent authority is indicated on the official cantonal portal (www.vs.ch) or at the municipality of residence.
Step-by-step of the request:
1. **Gather documentation**: [cantonal tax return](nav:tax-return) for the last two years (extract of taxable income and taxed assets), pay slip or certificate of self-employed income, certificate of family composition from the municipality.
2. Check income limits: contact the competent cantonal office and obtain the exact access criteria for the current year (a couple without children with a joint taxable income up to CHF 80,000–100,000 can generally access the reduction, depending on local parameters).
3. Submit application: fill out the reduction request form (usually available online on the Valais portal or at the municipal office) and send it by post or in digital format.
4. Decision and payment: the office evaluates the request within about 4–6 weeks and communicates the monthly subsidy amount. The contribution is paid directly to the selected insurer, reducing the premium due.
5. Annual renewal: the reduction is granted for the calendar year; by December 31, it is necessary to renew the request if the income conditions remain unchanged.
### Deadlines and change of health insurance
The deadline to change health insurance is December 31 of each year, effective from January 1 of the following year. The notice of termination from the old insurer must be received by the insurer by that date, preferably by registered mail or through the online portal. If the reduction is approved, it is advisable to communicate the grant number or the estimated contribution to the new health insurance to avoid incorrect billing.
Those who do not change insurers by December 31 automatically renew the annual contract on the same policy; in this case, the premium is fixed until December 31 of the following year (premium changes are valid only at the contract expiration).
Practical advice: check the premium list of available insurers in Valais at least three months before the deadline, both for the basic model and for alternatives (HMO, network), to evaluate which combination (insurer + deductible + model + estimated reduction) offers the lowest total annual cost.

item.title: Residence Permit B Freiburg: Requirements and Renewal
item.description: Permit B in Freiburg: requirements for EU/EFTA and third countries, renewal procedures, necessary documents and roles of the SEM and cantonal administration.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The B permit is a renewable residence permit for foreigners in Switzerland - The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) regulates the criteria at the federal level - Renewal: the concrete procedures are managed by the Fribourg cantonal administration - Documents and requirements vary for EU/EFTA citizens and third countries
## Key facts - **What**: B residence permit — renewable residence and work permit - Who: State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) — federal authority - Where: Canton of Fribourg — cantonal migration administration - Duration: Renewable according to federal and cantonal decisions - Category: EU/EFTA foreigners and third countries
The B permit is the most common residence permit for those living and working in Switzerland, including the Canton of Fribourg. Unlike the L permit (short duration up to one year), the B permit is renewable and allows for a more stable stay in the Swiss territory. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), a federal body, establishes the general criteria and competencies; however, the concrete procedures for application and renewal remain with the Fribourg cantonal administration.
### Who can apply for the B permit in Fribourg The legal status varies between citizens of the European Union and the European Free Trade Association (EU/EFTA) and foreigners from third countries. Both categories can access the B permit, but with sometimes different requirements and documentation. The main difference concerns access to the labor market and the conditions of stay in the territory: those with EU/EFTA status benefit from more favorable conditions compared to third countries.
General requirements include: having a confirmed job offer or a stable employment situation, demonstrating self-financing capacity, possessing [mandatory health insurance](nav:health), and complying with the stay conditions defined by the federal and cantonal authorities. The lack of one of these elements can result in the rejection of the application or a referral for clarification.
### The role of the Fribourg administration The Fribourg cantonal migration office manages practically all instances of application, renewal, and modification of the B permit. Although the fundamental regulations are issued by the SEM at the federal level, it is the cantonal administration that evaluates individual files, requests additional documentation, and issues the permit. For those residing or intending to move to Fribourg for work reasons, it is advisable to contact the Fribourg cantonal administration directly to know the updated forms, specific deadlines, and methods of submitting the file. ## Renewal of the B permit: procedures and timelines
Unlike other permit categories, the B permit is not unlimited: it has a fixed duration set by federal and cantonal authorities at the time of initial issuance. When this duration is about to expire, it is necessary to request a renewal from the competent cantonal administration, in this case, the offices of Fribourg. The renewal procedure generally follows the same guidelines as the initial application: it is necessary to demonstrate that the original conditions persist (employment, self-financing, [health insurance](nav:health)). However, the administrative process is sometimes more streamlined, as the authorities already have historical information about the applicant.
### How to obtain information on deadlines and procedures
The first step is to contact the cantonal administration of Fribourg directly. Online, it is possible to find: official forms for renewal, list of required documents (identity card, employment contract, health insurance certificate, criminal record extracts if necessary), cantonal and municipal administrative costs, and indicative processing times. This information is essential for planning the procedure in advance.
### Implications for those working and residing in Fribourg
For those who already hold a B permit and reside permanently in Fribourg for work reasons, renewal is a crucial aspect of medium-term planning. [Self-financing and cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) are factors that the administration evaluates carefully. A lack of timely renewal can lead to the loss of legal residence status and, consequently, to occupational and tax complications. It is therefore essential to schedule the expiration date and start the renewal procedure at least 2-3 months before the deadline to avoid bureaucratic delays.
### Third-country nationals vs. EU/EFTA citizens
An important practical difference concerns the times and documentation: EU/EFTA citizens generally benefit from faster administrative processes and less stringent documentation requirements. Third-country nationals may face longer duration assessments and additional clarification requests. The SEM provides general guidelines at the federal level; however, each canton (including Fribourg) applies small procedural variants. Consulting local authorities directly remains the most reliable strategy to comply with all prescriptions.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Practical checklist: how to proceed with the renewal
Here are the concrete steps for those who need to renew their B permit in Fribourg:
**1. Identify the expiration date**: Check the expiration date written on the current B permit. This is the absolute starting point.
2. Contact the Fribourg administration: Find the phone number and address of the Fribourg cantonal migration office through the official website of the canton.
3. Request the updated forms: Ask which are the official forms for renewal and the exact checklist of required documents.
4. Gather the documents: Generally, a valid passport or ID card, current employment contract or letters from the company confirming employment, Swiss health insurance certificate, residence certificate (sometimes issued by the municipality), documentation of income level if relevant, and criminal record extract (mandatory in some cantons) are required.
5. Submit the complete dossier: Start the renewal procedure at least 2-3 months before the expiration date. Submit the complete dossier to avoid requests for additional information that prolong the process.
6. Monitor the status of the application: The administration will communicate the status of the application by mail or email. Respond promptly to any requests for clarification.
7. Pick up the new permit: Once approved, the new B permit will be available for pickup at the cantonal office.
### Tools for planning self-financing
If you are a resident in Switzerland and want to calculate your tax obligations or better understand your net salary (a crucial element to demonstrate self-financing during renewal), you can use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator). This tool helps plan the economic management of your stay in Switzerland and document the income level required by the administration.
### When to contact a specialized consultant
If your personal situation is complex (imminent change of employer, previous permits with particular histories, family situations with dependents), it is advisable to consult a Swiss immigration law expert before submitting the renewal. A consultant can verify that your documentation is complete and that there are no procedural obstacles.
Keep your documents always up-to-date and monitor the permit deadlines with precision. To receive monthly information on permits, taxation, and job opportunities in Switzerland, [access the Frontaliere Ticino calculator](nav:calculator).

item.title: Nursery: gaps in controls on minors
item.description: An educator reported for child pornography worked in a kindergarten for two years. How and why institutional controls failed in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A kindergarten educator reported in 2024 for pedopornographic interests - Continued to work undisturbed until arrest in July 2026 - Criminal record remained clean, no ban on contact with minors
## Key facts - **What**: Report of online pedopornographic interests not followed by preventive actions - When: January 2024 (report); June 2026 (critical episode); July 2026 (arrest) - Where: Kindergarten in Saint-Sulpice (Canton Vaud) - Who: An educator, Federal Police, Public Prosecutor's Office of North Vaud, parents - Origin of report: National Center for Missing and Exploited Children - Initial outcome: No prosecution by the Public Prosecutor
In January 2024, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children reported to the Federal Police the online activities of a kindergarten educator in Saint-Sulpice (VD), which showed clear pedopornographic interests. The report was forwarded to the Public Prosecutor's Office of North Vaud, which however issued a no prosecution decision with a surprising justification: it was considered the "first complaint" and it was probably the case that the man "was not aware of acting illegally."
This decision had a critical consequence: the educator's criminal record remained clean. No criminal proceedings meant no ban on working with minors. And so, for two years, the man continued to operate in the public kindergarten without any restrictions.
### The first alarm from parents
At one point, the three-year-old son of a couple reported that an adult at the kindergarten had given him "kisses on the mouth and strokes on the head." The mother contacted the management of the facility, asking for reassurances about the professional profiles of the staff. According to the account in the newspaper 24heures, the management "seemed to doubt the child's words," even though they received the parents in repeated meetings over the following months. The parents emphasized that the child had never spoken negatively about the other educators, with whom he had a very good relationship; his reports always concerned the same man.
The most serious element emerged in June 2026: the child reported that the same man had touched his penis and shown him his own. At that point, investigators acted and the educator was arrested in July 2026. It was only during the subsequent investigations that the 2024 report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children emerged — a report that no one at the facility, the Municipality, or the Canton knew about.
### The void in coordination between institutions
What emerges from the case is an alarming picture of absent coordination between the Federal Police, the Cantonal Public Prosecutor's Office, the Canton of Vaud, and the Municipality of Saint-Sulpice. The Public Prosecutor's Office argued that, since no criminal proceedings had been opened (due to the no prosecution decision), it could not impose a ban on participating in activities involving contact with minors.
The Municipality of Saint-Sulpice stated to the newspaper that they knew nothing about it, adding that "they had received the green light from the Canton, which is responsible for checking criminal records." item.title: Zug inheritance tax: rates and exemptions
item.description: In the Canton of Zug, inheritance and gift taxes are cantonal matters. Spouse and descendant exemptions, kinship rates: how the declaration works.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Inheritance tax is a cantonal, not federal, matter in Switzerland - Spouses and direct descendants benefit from exemptions or reduced rates - Mandatory declaration within deadlines set by the canton - Each canton sets its own rates, updated periodically
## Key facts - **What**: Inheritance and gift tax - Where: Canton of Zug and all of Switzerland - Who: Heirs, beneficiaries of gifts, donors - Exemptions: Spouse, children, descendants according to cantonal legislation - Scope: Matter of cantonal law, decentralized tax management
In Switzerland, the taxation of inheritances and gifts is the exclusive responsibility of the Cantons. The Canton of Zug, like all other Swiss cantons, has enacted its own cantonal legislation that regulates the rates, exemptions, and declaration procedures for inheritances and gifts. Unlike many European countries, the Federal Council does not set uniform rates at the national level: each canton decides autonomously how and how much to tax the transfer of wealth between generations.
This federalist structure creates a variety of tax scenarios depending on the domicile of the deceased or the donor at the time of death or donation. For those residing in Zug, it is crucial to understand the specific regime of the canton, particularly the rates applied for degree of kinship (spouse, descendants, collaterals, strangers) and any possible exemptions or franchises.
### Why inheritance remains a cantonal matter
Inheritance and gift taxes constitute an important item in cantonal tax revenues, although less than income and property taxes. Their structure reflects principles of tax equity and family protection: in almost all cantons, the spouse and direct children benefit from total exemptions or significantly reduced rates. The federal direct tax, by comparison, affects the annual income of every Swiss resident according to the federal rate added to the cantonal multipliers. Inheritance taxes, on the other hand, are applied once at the time of wealth transfer and vary deeply from one canton to another. ### Exemptions and rates by degree of kinship
In the Swiss cantonal system, the degree of kinship is the first element that determines the amount of tax due. The cantonal legislator protects the close family with total or very favorable exemptions. In many cantons, the widowed spouse is completely exempt from inheritance tax on the assets inherited from the deceased spouse. Similarly, direct children (and their descendants, if the child has died) enjoy total exemptions or very low rates—often halved or even lower than those for non-direct relatives.
For more distant relatives (brothers, sisters, uncles, cousins), the rate increases progressively. For strangers (people with no kinship to the deceased), the rate is even higher. Furthermore, many cantons, including Zug, apply a tiered system based on the amount of the inheritance: exemptions are often provided for small amounts, and the rate increases for brackets of movable and immovable wealth.
### Gifts between living individuals
As for gifts, the treatment is sometimes more favorable than for inheritances (because the donor is still alive and can benefit from personal income tax deductions), or it is equated to the inheritance treatment. Here too, the spouse and children often receive exemptions or significant reductions. In Zug, as in other cantons, gifts are subject to declaration with the Cantonal Administration of Finance.
### Declaration procedure and deadlines
The inheritance declaration is a mandatory obligation: the heirs or the administrators of the estate must communicate to the cantonal tax office (in the case of Zug, the Cantonal Administration of Finance) the composition of the deceased's estate within the deadlines set by cantonal law. The deadlines vary from canton to canton, generally from three months to one year from the death.
During this phase, it is necessary to provide a detailed inventory of the assets (money, securities, real estate, valuable movable property) and debts of the deceased. The tax office applies the rates in force at the time of the declaration and notifies the taxation by means of a tax notice. The heir must pay the tax within the deadline indicated in the notice, otherwise late interest and possible administrative penalties will be applied.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Step-by-step procedure to declare the inheritance in Zug
If you are an heir or administrator of an inheritance in the Canton of Zug, the procedure to follow is structured in five essential steps:
1. Verify the declaration deadline. Check with the Canton of Zug's Financial Administration the deadline by which to submit the inheritance declaration. Generally, the deadline starts from the day of death. Failure to comply with the deadline results in penalties and interest.
**2. Gather complete documentation.** Collect the death certificate, the will (if any), the list of the deceased's assets, bank documents, stock certificates, real estate documents, life insurance policies, and any proof of debts or encumbrances on the assets.
3. Fill out the official declaration form. Use the form provided by the Zug cantonal tax office. The form includes separate sections for real estate, credits, liquid assets in current account or cash, securities, life insurance, valuable movable assets, debts, and burdens.
4. Submit the declaration within the deadline. Deliver the completed and signed declaration to the Canton of Zug's Financial Administration, preferably in person or by registered mail to have proof of receipt and official tracking.
5. Receive and verify the tax assessment notice. After administrative verification, the canton will issue a notice communicating the amount of tax due. Verify that the applied rates correspond to your degree of kinship and the exemptions and brackets provided by the current cantonal law.
### Where to find the specific rates of Zug
Since each canton periodically updates its rates (sometimes every year with adjustments), it is essential to consult directly with the Canton of Zug's Financial Administration to obtain the current rates for each degree of kinship, mobile and immobile wealth bracket, and any exemptions. You can find this information on the official website of the Canton of Zug or by contacting the competent office directly.
Furthermore, if the inheritance includes real estate in more than one canton (e.g., a property in Zug and one in Ticino), each canton will apply its rates to the share of assets located in its territory. item.title: Wages and the labour market in the canton of Zug: sectors and levels
item.description: Swiss labour market: how wage determination works between collective agreements, cantonal taxation and education levels.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - No federal minimum wage; some cantons provide it (including Canton Zugo) - Collective agreements determine wages for about 50% of Swiss workers - Federal + cantonal + municipal taxes reduce gross salary - Level of education (VET/maturity/degree) is a key factor in the salary scale
## Key facts - **What**: Wage determination (federal + cantonal + collective agreements) - Where: Each canton has its own laws (Canton Zugo included) - Who: Workers, unions, employers' associations, cantonal authorities - When: Biennial/triennial negotiations (contracts); annual taxation - Framework: FDF (federal) + cantonal + municipal (multiplier) - Hours: Max 45 hours/week (industry, offices, sales) or 50 hours (other sectors) - Holidays: Min 4 weeks (5 for those under 20) - Contributions: AHV/AI/IV 5.3%; AD/AC 1.1%; LAINF 0.7–1.5%
In Switzerland, there is no federal minimum wage. This is the first major difference compared to many other European countries: wage determination depends mainly on three factors — the federal regulatory framework, cantonal laws, and collective labor agreements. In Canton Zugo, as in every Swiss canton, this combination applies with its own local variables. Understanding how the Swiss labor market works is essential for anyone working or seeking employment in Switzerland.
The federal regulatory framework sets common minimum standards: maximum hours (45 hours per week for industry, offices, and sales; 50 hours for other sectors), minimum holidays (4 weeks, 5 for those under 20), maternity (14 weeks at 80% of salary with maternity allowance), paternity (2 weeks). These are the "pillars" that apply throughout Switzerland, from Canton Zugo to Ticino, from Valais to St. Gallen. But the real determinant of gross and net wages is the combination of collective agreements, local market dynamics, and cantonal tax regime.
### Collective agreements and wage determination
Collective labor agreements are negotiated between unions and employers' associations (or individual employers) that set minimum wages, working conditions, and benefits for entire sectors or professional categories. In Switzerland, about 50% of the dependent workforce is covered by collective agreements. When you receive a [pay slip](nav:payslip), you will see how your gross salary was calculated based on the collective agreement applied by your company.
A collective agreement can cover an entire sector (e.g., banking, insurance, hospitality, manufacturing) or a specific group of companies. Each contract specifies a minimum salary scale based on seniority, level of education, and professional role. For example, a collective agreement in the manufacturing sector might set a different minimum salary for someone with a VET (Vocational Education and Training) diploma compared to someone with a high school diploma or a university degree.
In Canton Zugo, as in other cantons, the main sectors (industry, finance, trade, services, healthcare) almost all have collective agreements in force. These agreements are renewed periodically (usually every 2-4 years) and reflect market dynamics, inflation, and economic conditions. When contracts are renegotiated, one of the main points of discussion between unions and employers is always the wage increase, with significant variations depending on the sector and economic period. If you work in a company that applies a collective agreement, you are covered by it even if you are not a union member (so-called "erga omnes effect" in many cantons).
For sectors where there is no collective agreement, remuneration is determined by individual negotiation and market conditions — the employer and the worker negotiate the salary and employment conditions directly.
## Cantonal taxation and impact on net salary
When an employer offers a gross salary, the worker does not receive the full amount declared. The difference between gross and net depends on two fundamental elements: social contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, unemployment insurance, accident insurance, possibly occupational insurance) and taxes (federal, cantonal and municipal).
In Switzerland, the tax system is structured on three levels: direct federal tax (DFI), cantonal taxes and municipal taxes. Each canton has its own municipal rates and multipliers — meaning that two workers with the same gross salary in different cantons will have significantly different net salaries. This applies to the Canton of Zug as well as to any other canton.
### Federal, cantonal and municipal taxation
The direct federal tax is uniform throughout Switzerland and follows the same progressive rates. However, the IFD is only the first level. In the Canton of Zug (as in every canton), the cantonal tax is added, which varies from canton to canton. To understand in detail how these rates work, see the [dichiarazione delle imposte](nav:tax-return) guide, which explains the federal and cantonal system. In addition, each municipality in the canton of Zug applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax, which further amplifies the variations between municipalities. Knowing how the Swiss job market works is the first step; knowing where to find concrete information is the second. If you work or are looking for a job in the Canton of Zug (or in any other canton), there are specific tools and resources to check the salaries in your sector, understand the current collective agreements, and calculate your net income.
The cantonal employment office of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Wirtschaft, Abteilung Arbeit) publishes data and statistics on the local job market. At the national level, the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) and SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) provide detailed surveys on median salaries by sector, level of education, and Swiss region. A very useful tool is the SECO Salary Portal, which allows you to compare average salaries by profession and region. If you are looking for a current collective agreement in your sector, contact the main union in your professional field or the relevant employers' association. Even if you are not unionized, the collective agreement often applies anyway: a company that applies a collective agreement must guarantee at least the minimum conditions provided by the agreement to all workers (including non-members).
### Calculate your net salary and negotiate consciously
Once you know the proposed gross salary (or your current salary), it is essential to understand how much you will take home net. The [salary calculator](nav:calculator) allows you to enter your annual gross income, your canton of residence, and your municipality, and it automatically calculates federal, cantonal, and municipal taxes, as well as social contributions. This tool is invaluable when you want to: evaluate a job offer (compare salaries in different cantons), plan your available income for your family budget, understand the impact of inflation and contract renewals on your actual paycheck.
When negotiating a salary, always do so based on official market data. If you know the average salary for your profession, experience, and level of education in your canton (thanks to UST/BFS data), you will have a solid starting point for your research and negotiations. In sectors with a collective agreement, there is often less room for individual negotiation — the salary is already set by the agreement — but for senior positions, specialized roles, or those without an applicable collective agreement, negotiation is the standard. Remember that the first year of employment is a critical period: in Switzerland, during the first year, the employer can terminate the contract with one month's notice, making post-hiring negotiation less effective than before signing.
Understanding the Swiss job market — from how collective agreements work to the cantonal tax variations — is crucial for making informed decisions about your career. Each canton has its own peculiarities, and the Canton of Zug, while one of the most economically dynamic in Switzerland, follows the same federal rules as any other canton. If you are looking for a job or want to evaluate an offer, start exploring the market in your sector with official data (UST, SECO, unions) and use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to see your realistic net income. Knowledge and transparency are your best allies in negotiating fair working conditions in any Swiss canton.

## In short - The Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States proposes 517 million francs for Swiss farmers. - The free trade agreement with Mercosur is at risk after the rejection by the National Council. - The left threatens a referendum if deforestation and forced labor are not excluded.
## Key facts - **What**: Proposal of 517 million francs for Swiss farmers. - When: Discussion in autumn. - Where: Council of States. - Who: Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States. - Amount: 517 million francs.
The Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States is ready to make an important concession to Swiss farmers to save the free trade agreement with Mercosur countries. On Friday, it expressed its support for granting just over half a billion francs to Swiss producers. The agreement will now be discussed by the full chamber of the Council of States during the next session, following the rejection by the National Council last June. The left maintains the threat of a referendum.
In June, the farmers' lobby exerted its political weight to derail the agreement negotiated between the European Free Trade Association countries (Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, and Iceland) and Mercosur at the National Council. An agreement born after 8 years of negotiations, seen as an important outlet for Swiss products on a market of 270 million people, but perceived as a danger by Swiss farmers and livestock breeders, who fear heavy losses due to the arrival of low-cost products with lower standards than those required of them.
### Implications for Swiss Agriculture
The proposal by the Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States to grant 517 million francs to Swiss farmers represents an attempt to balance the concerns of the agricultural sector with the economic interests linked to the free trade agreement with Mercosur. This amount, although lower than the over 800 million francs requested by the agricultural world, is significantly higher than the 158 million francs provided by the Federal Council.
The issue goes beyond Mercosur; it is about supporting the concept of an economic policy based on free trade agreements to promote our exports. The Council of States will vote in the autumn session starting on September 14, and the proposal should gather the necessary votes to send a compromise to the National Council that would turn many "no" votes from the right into "yes" votes, leaving the left in the minority.
If the Amazon rainforest and forced labor are excluded from the agreement, the referendum remains on the table, as indicated by the Social Democratic Party councilor from Solothurn, Franziska Roth. Proposals to ban the import of goods produced, wholly or partly, with forced labor and to adopt the EU's deforestation regulations were both rejected, with 9 votes to 4 and 8 votes to 4 with 1 abstention, respectively.
The final word on the free trade agreement with Mercosur countries could then be up to the people. ## Practical Analysis
The free trade agreement with Mercosur represents a significant challenge for Swiss agriculture. Swiss farmers and livestock breeders fear that the arrival of low-cost products with lower standards could jeopardize their economic sustainability. The proposal of the Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States to grant 517 million francs to Swiss producers is an attempt to mitigate these concerns.

Before the Committee's proposal, the Federal Council had planned only 158 million francs to support Swiss farmers. The new proposal represents a significant increase, although it does not reach the over 800 million francs requested by the agricultural world. This increase could help compensate for potential losses due to competition from imported products from Mercosur.
### Possible Scenarios
If the free trade agreement with Mercosur is approved with the conditions proposed by the Committee, Swiss farmers would receive significant financial support. However, the left has threatened a referendum if deforestation and forced labor are not excluded. This could lead to a popular vote that will decide the fate of the agreement.
### Implications for the Swiss Economy
The free trade agreement with Mercosur could open new opportunities for Swiss exports but also create challenges for the agricultural sector. The Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States is seeking to find a balance between these conflicting interests by proposing financial support for Swiss farmers.
### Conclusion
The proposal of the Foreign Policy Committee of the Council of States to grant 517 million francs to Swiss farmers is an important step towards safeguarding the free trade agreement with Mercosur. However, the threat of a referendum by the left and concerns about deforestation and forced labor could further complicate the situation.

## In brief - Trial in Zurich for six members of 'Junge Tat' - Charges of discrimination and incitement to hatred - Prosecutor seeks prison sentences for main defendants
## Key facts - **What**: Trial for discrimination and incitement to hatred - When: Today - Where: Zurich - Who: Six members of 'Junge Tat' - Amount: Prison sentences requested
Today, six members of the far-right group 'Junge Tat' appeared before Zurich's justice system on charges of discrimination and incitement to hatred. During the hearing, the prosecutor requested prison sentences for the two main defendants, while the defense called for their acquittal. Outside the courthouse, about a hundred anti-fascist protesters gathered. The verdict will be pronounced only later.
This morning, the Public Prosecutor's Office requested a prison sentence of fifteen months, with six months to be served, against the two main defendants, Tobias Lingg (23) and Manuel Corchia (25). According to the prosecution, their actions exceeded the limits of freedom of expression. Both recidivists, they refused to answer the judge's questions.
In the afternoon, their defense lawyers instead asked for their clients to be acquitted of charges of discrimination, incitement to hatred, and violation of freedom of belief and worship. They invoked freedom of expression. According to Lingg's lawyer, the group's leader should only be sentenced to a conditional fine for minor offenses. For Corchia, complete acquittal was requested.
The first incriminating episode dates back to June 2022, when masked individuals attempted to disrupt a mass at the Church of Saints Peter and Paul during Pride, with the aim of placing a 2.4-meter-tall white wooden cross on a cement base with the inscription 'Nopridemonth' (literally no to a month of pride parade) inside the building. According to the prosecution, this way they disturbed the religious celebration, ridiculed the attendees, and caused damage to the stone floor of nearly 9,000 francs. The prosecution evaluates this action as discrimination based on sexual orientation and violation of freedom of worship and religion.
The second episode, which occurred in October of the same year, refers to a disturbance during a reading by drag queens intended for children at the Tanzhaus in Zurich. Three people who entered the building, where about fifty people were present, secretly recorded some conversations and attempted to unfurl a banner. Outside the building, other group members lit fireworks, chanted slogans, and distributed leaflets. According to the indictment, the smoke and threatening behavior frightened the attendees so much that, out of fear, they were unable to leave the building.
The court also dealt with several unauthorized actions carried out on the roofs of various buildings. In November 2022, some group members climbed onto the roof of the main building of the Basel train station, unfurled a banner reading 'Expel criminals,' and set off smoke bombs. They acted similarly in April 2024 in Winterthur (ZH), where they hung a banner dedicated to the theme of repatriation on a building. As early as May 2022, they climbed onto a crane in Zurich.
Today the courtroom was packed. In addition to numerous journalists, members of 'Junge Tat' were present, as well as organizers of events disrupted by the far-right group. Outside, about a hundred people gathered before the trial began to protest against right-wing extremism.
As mentioned, at the end of the hearing, the Zurich District Court had not yet decided on the manner and date of the verdict. ## Practical Implications
The trial in Zurich against members of 'Junge Tat' raises important questions regarding freedom of expression and discrimination in Switzerland. The prosecution requested prison sentences for the two main defendants, Tobias Lingg and Manuel Corchia, while the defense invoked their acquittal, arguing that their actions fall within freedom of expression.
The group's actions, such as interrupting a Pride Mass and disrupting a children's reading, caused material and psychological damage. The prosecution assessed these actions as discrimination based on sexual orientation and violation of freedom of worship and religion.
The case highlights the tension between freedom of expression and the need to protect the rights of minorities. The final ruling of the Zurich District Court will be crucial in establishing the limits of freedom of expression in Switzerland.

The court also examined several unauthorized actions taken on the roofs of various buildings. In November 2022, some members of the group had climbed onto the roof of the main building of the Basel train station, unfurled a banner with the words' Expel criminals' and lit smoke bombs. They had acted in a similar way in April 2024 in Winterthur (ZH), where a banner dedicated to the theme of repatriation had been hung on a building.

## In brief - Teenagers pile objects on the tracks - Interregio derails at 110 km/h - Damage amounting to 141,369 francs - Trial in Winterthur
## Key facts - **What**: Objects piled on the tracks - When: February 19, 2023 - Where: Zurich - Who: Teenagers and SBB maintenance worker - Amount: 141,369 francs
The incident, which occurred on February 19, 2023, ended up in court. Among the teenagers involved was an SBB maintenance worker. Scooters, tires, barrels, and barriers were piled on the SBB tracks. A prank that, on a February night in 2023, turned into a serious danger for rail traffic: an Interregio hit the obstacles at about 110 km/h. The case came before the District Court of Winterthur.
A consequence with serious repercussions Four minors and a man, then 31 years old, removed various objects from a shed near the Wiesendangen station and from a construction site, piling them on a track. One of the teenagers, employed in SBB maintenance, allegedly reassured the others that the train could not derail.
Just before 9:30 PM, an Interregio traveling from Lucerne to Constance hit the obstacles at about 110 km/h. The locomotive lifted slightly off the tracks and emergency braking was applied. No one was injured, but about one hundred passengers had to be evacuated and rail traffic was interrupted for four hours. The damage bill? 141,369 francs and 15 cents.
It wasn't the first time The night before, two minors, the adult, and another man, then 18 years old, had placed a 97-kilogram motorcycle on the tracks. A passenger train hit it at 110 km/h, requiring the evacuation of the train and the closure of the track for several hours.
The four minors were tried separately. The man, now 35 years old and with cognitive limitations, and his accomplice, now 22 years old, appeared before the Winterthur Court.
Both stated that they remembered little of the episodes and had already expressed themselves during the investigations. However, they admitted to the material execution of the facts.
The defenses argued that the defendants did not expect the passage of passenger trains. During the first episode, the perpetrators were "completely drunk." For the 35-year-old, his reduced intellectual capacity and, according to a psychiatric report, his easy influence were also highlighted.
Suspended sentences The public prosecutor requested a suspended prison sentence of 15 months for the 22-year-old and a 24-month sentence for the 35-year-old. The 35-year-old's defense lawyer agreed with the request. The 22-year-old's lawyer, however, requested a suspended fine of 180 daily units.
The District Court of Winterthur found both defendants fully capable of understanding and willing at the time of the facts, despite possible alcohol intoxication and the cognitive limitations of the older one. The 22-year-old, involved only in the first night, was sentenced to a suspended prison sentence of 12 months for public traffic disruption and damage. The 35-year-old, as requested by the prosecution, received a 24-month prison sentence for repeatedly committing the offenses. Additionally, he has road traffic offenses on his record. The execution of the prison sentence is suspended in favor of outpatient treatment. ## Practical Implications The affair has raised important issues regarding railway safety and the responsibility of minors. Accidents caused significant disruptions in rail traffic, resulting in inconvenience to passengers and high costs for repairs. This case underlines the importance of preventive measures to avoid such dangerous situations.

Authorities must work with schools and families to promote a culture of responsibility and respect for public property.

item.title: Opening a business in the Canton of Vaud: registration and costs
item.description: Practical guide to registration and costs to start a business in the Canton of Vaud: legal forms, Trade Register, three-tier taxation and insurance obligations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Canton of Vaud requires registration with the Commercial Register for any activity - Three levels of taxation: federal (IFD/VAT), cantonal and municipal - Contribution obligations: AVS/AI, LPP/BVG, LAMal, accidents - Legal form determines liability, minimum capital and administrative burdens
## Key facts - **What**: Opening a commercial or professional activity - Where: Canton of Vaud (French-speaking Switzerland) - Who: Individuals, partnerships, corporations - Federal competence: AFC/ESTV (IFD, VAT) - Cantonal competence: Vaud Tax Administration (cantonal/municipal taxes) - Registration: With the Commercial Register (CR) of the canton
Starting an activity in the Canton of Vaud requires an initial crucial choice: the legal form. Whether it is a sole proprietorship, a general partnership, a limited partnership or a corporation, each structure entails different obligations in terms of taxation, insurance and administration.
Registration with the Commercial Register (CR) is the first mandatory step: without it, the activity cannot operate legally. Each legal form has specific registration procedures and generates costs that vary depending on the nature of the business and the estimated income. In the Canton of Vaud, as in the rest of Switzerland, the tax system operates at three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal. This means that the new entrepreneur will have to fulfill tax obligations with three different administrations.
In addition to taxation, those who hire employees or work as self-employed must comply with important contribution obligations. Professional pension (LPP/BVG) and mandatory health insurance (LAMal) are non-negotiable requirements for anyone operating in Switzerland. The payment of AVS/AI/IPG contributions is also mandatory for any activity, regardless of the chosen legal form.
### Legal forms and liability
The choice of legal form determines the degree of personal liability, the tax burden and the administrative obligations. For a sole proprietorship (self-employed), no minimum capital is required and registration is relatively simple. The owner is personally liable for the company's debts with his personal assets. This form is ideal for freelancers and small businesses. Taxes are calculated on the net income of the activity, possibly added to other income of the individual.
A general partnership (GP) or a limited partnership (LP) involves joint and several liability of the partners (except the limited partner in the LP). These models are suitable for partnerships between professionals. No formal minimum capital is required. A corporation (Corp.) offers the maximum protection of personal liability of the shareholders: these are only liable for the amount of capital contributed. Taxation occurs both at the company level and at the individual level (on dividends). Administrative obligations are more complex and include the keeping of certified accounts, shareholders' meetings and auditing.
### Three-level tax system
In the Canton of Vaud, as everywhere in Switzerland, taxation is structured on three levels, each with its own deadlines and declaration methods. Federal level (managed by AFC/ESTV): Includes federal direct tax (FDT) and value-added tax (VAT). VAT applies to almost all supplies of goods and services, except for certain regulated exceptions (e.g., rents, healthcare, educational services). FDT is a progressive tax on the income and profits of individuals and legal entities. Any business exceeding a certain turnover threshold must register with the AFC for VAT and manage periodic declarations.
Cantonal level (tax administration of the Canton of Vaud): Applies a cantonal tax on income and profits. The Canton of Vaud has its own multipliers and rates, different from other cantons. The rate is progressive and varies based on the net income of the business, with specific declaration deadlines for the canton. Municipal level (municipalities of the Canton of Vaud): Applies a municipal tax, usually calculated as a multiplier applied to the cantonal tax amount. This means that each municipality has its own multiplier, creating territorial variability even within the canton. The same business can have slightly different tax burdens depending on the municipality of residence.
This three-level structure implies that a business will have to pay taxes to three different administrations, with distinct deadlines and declaration methods for each.
### Mandatory contributions and insurance
Anyone employing staff or working as a self-employed individual must register and pay contributions to various entities, according to federal regulations that apply uniformly throughout Switzerland. AVS/AI/IPG (Old-age and disability insurance, loss of earnings compensation): Mandatory contribution for both employees and self-employed individuals. For employees: 5.3% borne by the worker, supplemented by the employer's rate for a total of 10.6%. For self-employed individuals: a rate proportional to net income, verifiable with the competent cantonal office.
LPP/BVG (Mandatory occupational pension scheme): Mandatory for employees from a certain salary threshold (coordinated salary). Rates vary by age group: 7% (25–34 years), 10% (35–44), 15% (45–54), 18% (55+ until the reference age). Self-employed individuals can also voluntarily register with a collective fund or a private pension institution. LAMal/KVG (Mandatory health insurance): Binding for all residents in Switzerland. Premiums are individual, not linked to income, and vary by canton and region. It is not a tax or a salary contribution but a private insurance with per capita premiums. Deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 depending on the chosen policy. In the Canton of Vaud, cantonal subsidies are available to reduce premiums based on income.
Accident insurance (LAINF/LAA): Mandatory for employers, with a rate ranging from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector of activity. Self-employed individuals can voluntarily insure themselves with SUVA or other authorized insurers.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure
Step 1: Choose the legal form The decision on the legal form is the foundation of the entire operation. Sole proprietorship, LLC, LLP, or corporation? Each model has different implications for personal liability, tax burden, and administrative complexity. Consulting an accountant or lawyer can help evaluate the most suitable structure for the business plan, number of partners, degree of risk, and growth objectives.
Step 2: Registration with the Commercial Register of the Canton of Vaud After choosing the legal form, the entrepreneur (or partners, if a company) must submit an application for registration with the Commercial Register of the canton. The required documents vary depending on the legal form but generally include: registration form (available at the cantonal RdC office), certificate of domicile or lease of business premises, copy of the identity documents of the partners/owners, partnership agreement (for partnerships or corporations), declaration of compliance with hygiene and safety regulations (if relevant).
Step 3: Registration with tax authorities Once registered with the RdC, the company receives a federal identification number (UID). With this number, it is mandatory to register with AFC/ESTV for federal direct tax and, if applicable, for VAT; register with the tax administration of the Canton of Vaud for cantonal taxes; check with the municipality for municipal registration obligations.
Step 4: Registration for social contributions Submit an application for registration with the competent cantonal office for AVS/AI/IPG of the self-employed; if employees are hired, register with the cantonal labor office for contractual obligations; subscribe to a LPP insurance with a collective fund or, for the self-employed, with a private pension institution; take out individual health insurance (LAMal) with a health insurance fund active in the canton.
**Step 5: Insurance and compliance** Check the need for professional liability insurance (mandatory by law in some sectors); if applicable, subscribe to accident insurance (LAINF); ensure that the premises comply with hygiene and workplace safety regulations (SUVA).
### Key deadlines The deadlines vary depending on the legal form and activity, but some are fixed and non-negotiable:
- RdC registration: as soon as possible, ideally before the start of the activity - Federal tax registration: within 30 days of RdC registration - Cantonal registration: within the times indicated by the cantonal administration (usually 30–60 days) - AVS/AI contribution payment: calculated and paid quarterly according to fixed deadlines throughout the year - [Federal tax return](nav:tax-return): by March 31 of the following year of the tax period - Cantonal declaration: deadlines vary by canton (check with the Vaud administration)
### Useful resources and tools To navigate Swiss and cantonal bureaucracy, reliable resources are available: the official website of the Canton of Vaud (www.vd.ch) with information on tax registrations and procedures; the federal portal (www.admin.ch) for rules on federal direct tax, VAT, AVS/AI, and labor regulations; UST/BFS for statistical data on the number of companies and economic trends; the cantonal office for economy and labor (DIME or equivalent in Vaud).
Those who need an estimate of the total costs (registrations, monthly contributions, initial insurance premiums) can use the [business cost calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate different income scenarios or consult the cantonal tax administration directly, which provides free and non-binding estimates.

item.title: Franco-euro: what the data says
item.description: Swiss inflation 0.4%, Eurozone 2.9%: economic divergence between SNB and ECB exchange rate guide. Implications for border workers, businesses, and families.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - SNB keeps rates near zero, Swiss inflation contained at 0.4% - Eurozone records inflation at 2.9%, ECB adopts restrictive policy - Economic divergence influences euro-franc exchange rate in the coming months
## Key facts - **What**: Monthly analysis of the euro-franc exchange rate through Currency Watch - When: First part of the year: franc strengthened; subsequently euro recovery - Where: Switzerland vs Eurozone - Who: Swiss National Bank (SNB), European Central Bank (ECB) - Swiss Inflation: 0.4% - Eurozone Inflation: 2.9% - Analysis Platform: Forecaster.biz - Factors: Central banks, seasonality, positioning of large investors
The relationship between the Swiss franc and the euro continues to be a particularly important topic not only for those following financial markets but also for families, cross-border workers, and businesses that daily manage income, expenses, or liquidity in both currencies.
According to Currency Watch, the monthly appointment of CambiaValute.ch dedicated to the analysis of the foreign exchange market, the keys to understanding the exchange rate trend lie in the decisions of central banks and macroeconomic factors. The analyses use data processed through Forecaster.biz, a professional platform for quantitative analysis of financial markets.
### The economic divergence between Switzerland and the Eurozone
The economic situation between Switzerland and the Eurozone presents very different scenarios. In Switzerland, inflation remains contained around 0.4%. This dynamic has allowed the Swiss National Bank to keep interest rates at levels close to zero.
On the contrary, in the euro area, inflation stands at around 2.9%, driven in particular by the increase in energy costs. Faced with this situation, the European Central Bank has adopted a more restrictive monetary policy, intervening on interest rates.
This divergence has had direct consequences also on the foreign exchange market. In the first part of the year, the franc had benefited from the search for safety by investors, strengthening in conjunction with the increase in geopolitical tensions. Subsequently, the different orientation of the central banks has contributed to favor a recovery of the euro. ### How the exchange rate affects cross-border workers, businesses, and families
The Swiss franc-euro exchange rate is not just a numerical fluctuation: for cross-border workers who receive salaries in EUR, it has a direct impact on their purchasing power in Swiss francs. When the euro weakens against the franc, the actual value of the salary decreases. Conversely, when the euro strengthens, the cross-border worker experiences a real gain in terms of purchasing power.
For Swiss exporting companies, the exchange rate affects international competitiveness. A strong franc makes them less competitive in European markets; a weak franc favors exports.
For Swiss families, the exchange rate influences the cost of products imported from the Eurozone and the budget for travel in Europe. Additionally, the Swiss National Bank's monetary policy with interest rates close to zero affects mortgages, loans, and the returns of Swiss savers. Those with a savings account in CHF see very low returns; those financing a mortgage, however, benefit from reduced rates.
### The factors behind exchange rate fluctuations
According to Currency Watch, the main factors influencing the exchange rate in the coming months are three: the decisions of central banks, the seasonality of currency flows, and the positioning of large investors. Going beyond daily fluctuations means observing what happens behind the scenes.
The divergence between the SNB's policy (low rates, controlled inflation) and the ECB's policy (higher rates, sustained inflation) creates incentives for investors to shift capital towards the Eurozone, favoring the euro. Those managing liquidity in both currencies must consider these elements to make informed decisions on the best time to make currency transactions.
Currencies, as the analysis reminds us, are often one of the best thermometers of what is happening in the international economy and geopolitics.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to Follow the Evolution of the Franc-Euro Exchange Rate
For those who want to understand the evolution of the exchange rate and the macroeconomic factors behind the fluctuations, Currency Watch by CambiaValute.ch is a useful tool. It is a monthly analysis that examines the foreign exchange market through macroeconomic, statistical, and quantitative data, helping to read beyond the simple daily fluctuations.
The Forecaster.biz platform, used to generate the data and charts of the analyses, offers a quantitative perspective on financial markets. The available charts and statistical analyses allow you to visualize historical trends and identify recurring patterns in the exchange rate.
For those who want to monitor the exchange rate in real-time, a [comparison of exchange rates](nav:exchange) is available, showing current rates and allowing you to plan currency conversions.
### Concrete Strategies for Cross-Border Workers and Businesses
If you are a cross-border worker who receives a salary in EUR and spends in CHF, consider these steps:
1. Monitor the decisions of the SNB: The official statements of the Swiss National Bank on the meetings of the Governing Board provide indications on Swiss monetary policy and future interest rates.
2. Follow inflation data: The Swiss consumer price index published monthly by the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) vs. the European one offers a view of the economic divergence that fuels the exchange rate.
3. Use analysis tools: Platforms like Currency Watch provide processed data to make more informed decisions compared to simple daily quotes.
4. Distribute the timing: If possible, do not make all conversions in a single transaction. Distributing conversions over time reduces the risk of unfavorable exchange rates and allows you to benefit from any positive variations.
### CTA: Calculate the Impact of the Exchange Rate on Your Income
For cross-border workers who want to understand concretely how the euro-franc exchange rate impacts their net salary and purchasing power, it is possible to simulate the effect using a dedicated tool. [Access the salary calculator](nav:calculator) to see how exchange rate variations influence your income and plan your currency conversions more informedly.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/newsblog/valute-e-frontiere/1947998/franco-euro-cosa-dicono-i-dati-e-quali-prospettive-si-aprono-per-i-prossimi-mesi)*

item.title: Vaud canton transport subscriptions: zones and rates
item.description: Monthly, annual, half-price and General Subscriptions in Swiss public transport. How fare zones and student discounts work.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Tariff zones organize Swiss public transport for geographical areas - Monthly and annual subscriptions reduce costs for commuters and regular users - Half-fare (ARZ) and General Abonnement (AG) offer integrated national solutions - Special discounts available for students, apprentices, and protected categories
## Key facts - **What**: Subscription systems and tariff zones in Swiss public transport - Where: Canton Vaud and Swiss national network (trains, buses, trams, boats) - Who: Public transport operators, tariff communities, cantonal agencies - Tools: Zonal subscriptions, ARZ, AG, categorized offers - Categories: Students, apprentices, workers, retirees, people with disabilities
Swiss public transport, including Canton Vaud, is organized around tariff zones that delimit geographical areas of validity for tickets and subscriptions. This system allows passengers to plan their trips with tariff transparency and operators to structure revenues sustainably. A tariff community is an association of public entities and transport companies that coordinates fares, schedules, and offers across multiple zones, often covering several cantons.
### How tariff zones work The principle is simple: the ticket price depends on the number of zones crossed. Those traveling within a single zone pay less than those crossing three or five zones. This model encourages the purchase of commuter subscriptions, as the per-trip cost is significantly reduced compared to single tickets. Zones are geographically delimited and marked on public maps; each major city or region has its own zonal structure.
### Monthly, annual, and combined subscriptions Monthly subscriptions cover 30–31 consecutive days and allow unlimited travel within the chosen zones. An annual subscription commits for 12 months and is economically more advantageous on a pro-rata basis. Many networks also offer shorter-term subscriptions (quarterly, semi-annual) for intermediate needs. The choice between monthly and annual depends on the stability of one's travel: those certain of using public transport for at least 11–12 months should opt for the annual subscription. ### Half-price (ARZ) and General Abonnement (AG): integrated solutions Two Swiss national tools expand the savings options beyond the zonal subscriptions. The **Half-price** (ARZ – Abonnement Réduction Zéro in French) is a permanent 50% discount applied to single tickets and subscriptions of all participating networks (national railways, regional buses, trams, funiculars, boats). It is not an independent subscription but a tariff reduction tool. Those who possess ARZ purchase discounted versions of the same products. The General Abonnement (AG) represents the highest level of tariff integration. It is a single card that allows unlimited travel on the entire Swiss public transport network (trains, buses, trams, funiculars, boats) for 365 consecutive days, regardless of zones. The AG completely eliminates the geographical constraint and is convenient for those who make long, variable, or frequent trips between different cantons. ### Discounts for students and apprentices Students regularly enrolled in schools, high schools, universities, and apprentices with a valid contract fall into privileged categories in the Swiss public transport system. The reductions typically vary between 20% and 50% compared to regular fares, depending on the network and the managing entity. Access requires the presentation of an updated school enrollment document or apprenticeship contract. The cantonal public transport administrations publish the annual tariffs and access conditions for these categories. ### Economic impact on the family budget For a worker who commutes daily between zones, the cost of public transport significantly impacts the monthly budget. A conscious choice of subscription — zonal, ARZ, or AG — can reduce this expense by 30–50% compared to single tickets. There is no universally optimal option, but a personalized comparison between one's mobility habits and available fares allows identifying the most convenient solution. ### Additional cantonal contributions Some cantons, including Vaud, offer direct subsidies to subscriptions for specific categories (low-income families, people with disabilities, workers in vulnerable situations). These contributions are administered by the cantonal authorities and are added to the tariff discounts. It is advisable to verify with the competent cantonal office if one falls into a privileged group.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Procedure to choose the right subscription The selection process is pragmatic and requires a few steps:
**1. Map your routes** — Identify the geographical areas where you travel regularly (work, school, recurring activities).
2. Count the days of use — How many days do you actually use public transport each month? Those who travel 20+ days/month benefit more from a monthly or annual subscription compared to single tickets.
3. Compare official price lists — Access the local fare community website (e.g., TL for Lausanne/Vaud) and consult the current prices for zonal subscriptions, half-price, and General Abonnement.
4. Evaluate ARZ and AG — If your travels include multiple cantons or long distances, calculate whether the annual cost of ARZ or AG is lower than the sum of the zonal subscriptions you would have purchased separately.
5. Check for subsidized categories — If you are a student, apprentice, retiree, disabled, or fall into a subsidized category, check the applicable discounts and required documents.
6. Purchase and set up renewal — Many networks allow online purchase, via mobile app, or at physical sales points. Automatic renewal is available for annual subscriptions.
### Timing and deadlines Monthly subscriptions follow the natural calendar (from the first to the last day of the month). Annual subscriptions start from the activation date and expire exactly 12 months later. Renew a few days in advance to avoid service interruptions. Many networks offer a tolerance window (2–5 days) for renewal without loss of coverage.
### Calculation tools and advice For a complete assessment of your monthly budget in Switzerland, public transport represents a significant expense alongside rent, food, and insurance. Use the [cost of living calculator](nav:cost-of-living) to simulate the economic impact of different mobility choices (zonal subscription vs. ARZ vs. AG vs. private means) on total monthly expenses.
Next step: Visit the fare portal of your canton's fare community, download the updated price list, and simulate the annual cost of the subscription best suited to your mobility profile. If you remain uncertain, contact the customer service of the transport network for personalized and free advice.

item.title: AVS and complementary services: Vaud
item.description: How the first pillar works in the Canton of Vaud. Cantonal Compensation Fund Guide, Contribution Gaps and Supplementary Benefits for Minimum Living.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - AVS: 5.3% employee contribution; retirement age 65 for men - PC: cantonal benefits to cover the minimum living standard when the pension is insufficient - Vaud Compensation Fund: manages contributions, pension calculations, and PC access
## Key facts - **What**: Three-pillar pension system; AVS is the mandatory first national pillar - Who: UFAS/BSV (federal office), Vaud cantonal compensation fund - Where: Canton Vaud, French-speaking Switzerland - When: Contributions throughout working life; pension from the set date - Amount: 5.3% gross employee, 5.3% employer; self-employed 10.6% on net income
In Canton Vaud, the Swiss pension system is structured into three pillars: the first is AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance), the second is LPP (mandatory occupational pension), and the third is individual private savings. The Vaud cantonal compensation fund is the administrative body that manages, at the local level, the inflow of AVS contributions, the calculation of pensions, and support for supplementary benefits (PC).
AVS is a mandatory scheme for anyone working or residing in Switzerland. An employee pays 5.3% gross of their salary as an AVS/AI/IPG contribution (covering old age, disability, maternity allowance). The employer pays an additional 5.3%, totaling 10.6% of the wage bill. Self-employed individuals pay 10.6% on their net income from self-employment, in two semi-annual installments.
Supplementary benefits are a cantonal mechanism that supplements the AVS pension amount when it does not cover the minimum living standard: rent, food, essential healthcare. In Vaud, eligibility for PC depends on total income, assets, and family composition. Unlike the AVS pension, which is calculated at the federal level according to a standardized formula, PC varies by canton because each canton sets its own income and asset limits.
### Role of the compensation fund in Vaud The Vaud cantonal compensation fund is one of the nine administrative branches of the Swiss AVS system. It receives payments from employers and employees, records them in personal contribution files, calculates pensions at the retirement date according to formulas set by UFAS/BSV, and manages files for PC access. When a person approaches retirement age (65 for men under current regulations), the Vaud fund automatically sends them a communication summarizing the contributions made and a preliminary estimate of the future pension. This document is crucial: it allows the future retiree to identify any contribution gaps and take corrective action before applying for the pension.
To learn more about the Swiss pension system, consult the [complete guide to the first pillar and pensions](nav:pension). ### Contributory gaps: nature and recoverability
A contributory gap arises when a year of insurance has no contributions or only partial ones. The causes can be involuntary — periods of unemployment, maternity/paternity leave, illness, injury — or voluntary, such as a work interruption for personal reasons. The good news is that many gaps are recoverable. The Vaud cantonal compensation fund allows for retroactive contributions to be paid within certain deadlines and under specific conditions. Those who were unemployed and received unemployment benefits (AD/AC) will have automatic contributions credited by the unemployment fund. Those on maternity leave benefit from contributions covered by the health insurance fund or the institution that provided the subsidy.
Voluntary gaps — years in which you did not work by choice — are harder to fill: the payment is optional and must be actively requested from the fund. Only the last 10 years of voluntary gaps can generally be recovered, at the discretion of the compensation fund.
### Pension calculation: formula, indices, and impact
The AVS pension is not calculated as a simple percentage of the average salary. The formula considers:
1. **Number of contribution years**: from a minimum of 1 year up to 44 years for full pension entitlement. Those with fewer than 44 contribution years receive a proportionally reduced pension. 2. Average annual salary: determined based on contributions paid throughout the working life, updated each year according to the salary index published by UFAS/BSV. 3. Salary index: UFAS/BSV updates this index annually to reflect national salary inflation. The pension amount is revalued each year.
If contribution years are missing, the pension is proportionally reduced. For those with gaps, retroactive recovery increases the calculated average salary and thus the future pension. A hypothetical scenario: a person with 5 contributory gaps, if not recovered, will see a reduction in the pension compared to someone with 44 complete years. If the gaps are filled through retroactive payments before retirement, the recognized average salary increases and the future pension grows accordingly.
### Supplementary benefits: access criteria
The Vaud compensation fund approves requests for supplementary benefits according to maximum income and asset criteria set by the canton. For example, the total annual income (including AVS pension, residual work income, family allowances if any) must not exceed a certain threshold. Similarly, the liquid assets (bank accounts, securities, real estate not used as primary residence) must not exceed a maximum. The criteria vary by canton: Vaud has its own ceilings, different from other cantons.
An [interactive calculator](nav:calculator) helps you estimate your pension based on your contribution data.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure to request supplementary benefits in Vaud
The process is administrative, managed by the Vaud cantonal fund. Here's how it proceeds:
1. Contact the fund well in advance Don't wait until the day of retirement. Contact the Vaud cantonal compensation fund well before the expected retirement date. During this interview (often available via videoconference), the fund verifies if you are eligible for supplementary benefits based on your estimated income and declared assets.
**2. Gather the necessary documents** Prepare to provide: contribution extract (automatically provided by the fund); documents of total income (tax forms, self-employment income certificates if applicable); rental contract or property certificate of the residence; lists of current expenses (utilities, insurances); asset declarations (bank statements, securities balances).
3. Complete the official request The fund provides a standardized form for the supplementary benefits application. It is not particularly complicated, but it must be filled out accurately: full names, dates of birth, account numbers, income and asset amounts declared exactly.
4. Send the application to the Vaud fund You can send the application by regular mail to the fund's address, or deposit it directly at the cantonal offices if present in your municipality of residence. Always keep a copy for your personal records.
5. Wait for the decision The fund processes the application in times that vary depending on the administrative load; it is generally prudent to expect several weeks. If doubts arise about income, assets, or other information, the fund contacts you for clarification requests or additional documentation.
6. Approval and payment If the request is approved, the benefits start from the first day of the month following the decision (they are not, normally, retroactive; except in extraordinary circumstances and duly documented).
### Federal and cantonal support
The Vaud cantonal fund operates within the framework set by the UFAS/BSV, which establishes the national criteria for AHV and the guidelines for supplementary benefits. However, the total amount of SB, income and asset ceilings, and the administrative procedure vary by canton. Vaud, like every Swiss canton, has its own legislation on SB.
For official information on AHV and SB rights in the Canton of Vaud, contact the cantonal fund directly or visit the official website of the Canton of Vaud (cantonal administration > social welfare). Many municipalities in the Vaud territory also provide free consultation offices for retirees.
### Act before retirement
Do not postpone the check of contribution gaps. If you have had periods without regular payments (unemployment, maternity, work interruptions), contact the Vaud compensation fund immediately to verify your position. Free advice helps you understand if it is worth recovering gaps before the retirement date.
Contact the Vaud fund or consult the [AHV calculator for an estimate of the pension](nav:pension) and schedule a personalized interview with the fund.
